title: Oct 3 Results + Oct 4 Preview: Three Out of Four Ain't Bad
summary: 75% hit rate on Oct 3 with just one stumble in Cleveland. Tomorrow: back to Milwaukee.

content.value:
## Another Solid Day in the Books

You know, after doing this for more years than I care to count, a 3-1 day still feels pretty damn good. We've seen plenty of Octobers where the unexpected becomes routine, and yesterday was no exception. The model clicked on three fronts, stumbled once in Cleveland, and now we're looking ahead to Saturday's slate with that familiar mix of confidence and caution.

## The Cleveland Conundrum

Let's address the elephant in the room first. We liked the Guardians at 52% against the Sox, and that one didn't go our way. Here's the thing about October baseball that I've learned over the decades—tight probability picks in the postseason are coin flips wearing fancy statistical clothes. When you're at 52%, you're basically saying 'this could go either way, but we're leaning here.' Sometimes the coin lands on tails.

The other three? Chef's kiss. The Dodgers handled business at 65% confidence, the Rays came through at 59%, and Milwaukee—yeah, we'll talk more about Milwaukee in a minute—delivered at 53%.

## What Worked Yesterday

The Dodgers pick was the most comfortable of the bunch, and it showed. When you've got that kind of talent gap and the model gives you 65% confidence, you sleep easy. The Rays-Yankees game was fascinating—Tampa Bay continues to play spoiler in ways that remind me of their early 2000s scrappiness. Some things never change in baseball.

And Milwaukee... well, that brings us nicely to tomorrow.

## Tomorrow's Top Pick: Back to the Brew Crew

Here's where experience tells you something the spreadsheets won't: we're going right back to Milwaukee. I know what you're thinking—'Max, didn't they just play yesterday?' Yep. And we liked them then at 53%, they delivered, and now we like them again at 50% even.

This is basically a toss-up on paper, which makes the pitching matchup everything. Michael King takes the ball for San Diego—solid arm, been around, knows October. Logan Henderson counters for Milwaukee. The model sees this as dead even, which in my experience means home field advantage becomes the tiebreaker.

## The Veteran's Take

I've seen enough 50-50 games to know they're either going to make you look brilliant or foolish, with no in-between. But here's the thing about Milwaukee this October—they've got that quiet confidence you can't quite quantify. The kind of energy that reminds me of some of those Cardinals teams from the mid-2000s that just found ways to win at home.

King is good, no doubt. But Henderson at home, in October, with momentum from yesterday? I've seen this movie before. It usually ends with the home crowd going home happy.

We're riding with the Brewers again. Sometimes the best strategy is to dance with who brought you to the party.

## The Bottom Line

75% accuracy keeps the lights on and the confidence high. One miss in Cleveland doesn't erase three solid calls elsewhere. Tomorrow's a fresh slate, and we're leaning into a home team in a deadlocked matchup where intangibles matter as much as ERA.

That's baseball in October. That's why we love it.

*— Max*
